clue.text: They may be grating, but they are conservation minded

definitions.meaning: tools that scrape a surface make a harsh, rasping sound or literally grate
people who scrape and save are thrifty, keen to conserve their money

explanation.surface: Some irritating people turn out to care about the environment after all.
explanation.definitionFit: Scraping tools rasp across surfaces, while penny-pinchers scrape every coin together and waste nothing.

clue.text: Cast off-it's very muddy

definitions.meaning: to shed a skin, as a snake does
a swamp or boggy hollow full of mire

explanation.surface: Someone leaves a garment behind because it is filthy.
explanation.definitionFit: A snake sheds its skin this way, and the same word names a mire or bog.

clue.text: When students can revel in their scruffy clothing?

definitions.text: When students can revel in their scruffy clothing?

parts.words: When students can revel in their scruffy clothing?
parts.note: a charity fundraising festival held by British university students, read playfully as an occasion for wearing tatty clothes

explanation.surface: An occasion when undergraduates celebrate dressed like scarecrows.
explanation.walkthrough: In British universities this is the day of a student charity carnival; 'rag' also means a scrap of old cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: A student carnival day, with collections for charity, also suggests a day for wearing tatters.

clue.text: Places around the north building boats

indicators.note: around means the word for places is wrapped about the letter for north

parts.note: to place something is to put it
N is the abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: Shipyards up north are busy making vessels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'building' is a link word; 'boats' is the verb, as in going out on the river.
explanation.definitionFit: To go out in flat-bottomed river craft pushed with a pole is to go boating, so this word means boats.

clue.text: Dealing with bank refund

parts.note: re means concerning or regarding
a store or reserve, as in a blood bank

explanation.surface: An instruction concerning a bank paying money back.
explanation.definitionFit: To give back money taken is to return or reinstate it, as when a refund is made.

clue.text: Put much effort into accommodating voters

indicators.note: accommodating suggests adapting or adjusting, so the letters of the word voters are rearranged to fit

explanation.surface: A campaigner worked hard to win over and look after the electorate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accommodating' signals the anagram of VOTERS; 'into' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To strive is to try hard, so the past tense describes someone who made a great effort.

clue.text: Entrance for lorries?

definitions.meaning: the verb meaning to enrapture or delight
goods vehicles exist for carrying things from place to place

explanation.surface: A gateway set aside for heavy goods vehicles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Entrance' looks like a noun for a door; it is the verb en-TRANCE, to delight.
explanation.definitionFit: To enrapture someone is to carry them away with delight, and hauling goods by road is haulage.

clue.text: Better in an open-air school?

parts.note: outdoors, out of doors
a class is a group taught together

explanation.surface: Is it an improvement to hold lessons outdoors?
explanation.definitionFit: To surpass or beat someone easily is to better them.

clue.text: There's a steady drift at day's end

parts.note: even means steady or regular
a tide is a flow or current of water

explanation.surface: A calm current flows as the sun sets.
explanation.definitionFit: A poetic word for evening, the close of the day.

clue.text: When he plays he keeps stopping

definitions.text: When he plays he keeps stopping

parts.words: When he plays he keeps stopping
parts.note: the stops are knobs pulled on a church instrument with pipes, so a musician at its console is constantly working them

explanation.surface: A hesitant performer who can never get through a piece without pausing.
explanation.definitionFit: A keyboard player at a pipe instrument pulls stops to change the sound throughout a performance.

clue.text: Found the French male in a strong position

parts.note: to found metal is to cast it in a mould
le is the masculine form of 'the' in French

explanation.surface: A Frenchman discovered sitting pretty in a commanding post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Found' looks like the past of find; here it is the verb meaning to cast molten metal.
explanation.definitionFit: A fortified stronghold is a classic strong position, hard for attackers to take.

clue.text: A girl in overalls

indicators.note: in means the name lies within the letters of the word overalls

explanation.surface: A young woman dressed in work clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A common female first name, so it stands for a girl.

clue.text: Prime Minister lets go and goes to pieces

indicators.note: something that goes to pieces falls apart, so the letters of lets go and are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: A national leader loses his grip and has a breakdown.
explanation.definitionFit: William Gladstone served four terms as British premier in the Victorian era.

clue.text: Division in Croatia

definitions.meaning: a rift or schism between people or parts
a port city on the Dalmatian coast of Croatia

explanation.surface: A rift has opened up somewhere in the Balkans.
explanation.definitionFit: A rupture or schism is a division, and the same word names a historic Adriatic city in Croatia.

clue.text: A young attendant brought to book?

definitions.meaning: a boy servant at a court or a wedding
one leaf of a volume, part of what makes up a book

explanation.surface: A youthful servant is finally made to answer for his misdeeds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought to book' usually means punished; here it is read literally as something that goes into a book.
explanation.definitionFit: A boy who serves a noble or a bride is so called, and so is a single sheet within a printed volume.

clue.text: Tasty morsel served in pots at a get-together

indicators.note: a get-together puts things in a new arrangement, so the letters of in pots at a are mixed up

explanation.surface: Delicious nibbles dished up in bowls at a party.
explanation.definitionFit: Italian appetisers such as olives and cured meats are tasty starters served before a meal.

clue.text: Inspired article put back or employed

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

indicators.note: put back means the word or is turned to run the other way

parts.note: taken as written
employed means used

explanation.surface: An inspirational essay was either returned or put to use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inspired' reads like an adjective for the article, but it is the definition, in the sense of feelings stirred up; 'put back' turns only the little word 'or'.
explanation.definitionFit: Feelings that are inspired have been stirred up or awakened in someone.

clue.text: Upset over prohibition on the bicycle

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the first word sits above the second

parts.note: cross means angry or upset
a bar is a ban or prohibition

explanation.surface: Someone annoyed at a ban on cycling.
explanation.definitionFit: The horizontal tube joining a bike's saddle post to its handlebars is a part found on it.

clue.text: Affable country person without money

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside means the word for country person surrounds the money letter

parts.note: a peasant is a rural labourer
L stands for pound, the British unit of money

explanation.surface: A friendly rustic who has no cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like lacking, but here it means outside: PEASANT goes around L.
explanation.definitionFit: A pleasant person is friendly and agreeable, much like an affable one.

clue.text: Tells of churchmen being decapitated

indicators.note: losing the head means the word for churchmen drops its first letter

parts.note: prelates are senior clergy such as bishops

explanation.surface: A story about bishops losing their heads in a bloody purge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being decapitated' removes the P from PRELATES; 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To relate a story is to narrate or recount it, so someone who relates tells.

clue.text: The kind to arrange things

definitions.meaning: to put items in order or classify them

explanation.surface: The sort of person who likes to tidy up.
explanation.definitionFit: A sort is a type or variety, and to sort is to classify items into order.

clue.text: Opposed to some entrant in the big race

indicators.note: some means only part of the words entrant in is taken, the letters lying within them

explanation.surface: Someone against a particular runner in the Grand National.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'entrANT In'; 'the big race' only completes the picture of a horse race.
explanation.definitionFit: As a preposition or adjective, the word means against or hostile to something.

clue.text: Bill's found a number are of some importance

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a number
things that count matter or carry weight

explanation.surface: Bill discovers that a handful of people really matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' is not a man's name but an invoice; 'found' is a link meaning the pieces are discovered to make it.
explanation.definitionFit: An invoice or statement of money owed is an account.

clue.text: A fleshy-leafed, purple flowered plant or tree

parts.note: taken as written
a pine is a conifer tree

explanation.surface: A botanical guide asks whether something is a succulent or a conifer.
explanation.definitionFit: A stonecrop (Sedum telephium), also called livelong, is a succulent with purple flower heads.

clue.text: Spare silver put into a pool

indicators.note: put into means the silver symbol goes inside the word for pool

parts.note: a mere is a lake or pond
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Some spare coins are tossed into a pond.
explanation.definitionFit: Spare in the sense of scanty or lean means the same as thin and inadequate.

clue.text: Rogue will do badly

definitions.meaning: as a verb the word means to do work carelessly or skimp it

explanation.surface: A villain is bound to make a mess of the job.
explanation.definitionFit: A rascal is so called, and as a verb the same word means to skimp a task or do it hastily and poorly.

clue.text: A fast mover's chores are well-organised

indicators.note: organising things puts them into a new order, so the letters of chores are get rearranged

explanation.surface: A speedy worker gets the household jobs done efficiently.
explanation.definitionFit: A thoroughbred bred for the turf is built to gallop at great speed.

clue.text: One-man women

parts.note: a group of women belonging to a single man, as wives or concubines in a household

explanation.surface: Women devoted to a single partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One-man women' sounds like a phrase for faithful women, but it means many women kept by one man.
explanation.definitionFit: The women's quarters of a polygamous household, or its wives and concubines collectively, all belong to one man.

clue.text: One way to cook second-rate produce

parts.note: B grade is the second rank, below A
to raise crops or livestock is to produce them

explanation.surface: A cookery tip about using inferior vegetables.
explanation.walkthrough: 'produce' looks like a noun for vegetables; it is the verb meaning to grow.
explanation.definitionFit: Slow-cooking in a little liquid in a covered pot is a standard culinary method.

clue.text: Preparing a hot meal?

parts.note: a spicy Indian-style dish is being made, though the word also means grooming a horse or seeking favour

explanation.surface: Someone is busy in the kitchen making something spicy.
explanation.definitionFit: Making a spiced dish of meat or vegetables in sauce is literally what the word describes.

clue.text: No-one thanks right back for any allowance made

indicators.note: back tells us the whole run of pieces is read from the end to the start

parts.note: taken as written
the Roman numeral for one is I
ta is British informal for thank you

explanation.surface: Nobody is grateful for any concession that gets offered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses NO, I, TA and R together, giving the letters RATION; 'for any' and 'made' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A fixed quota of food or fuel issued to each person is an allowance.

clue.text: Dash impressed the egghead

parts.note: to impress a mark is to stamp it

indicators.note: the head of the word egg means its first letter

explanation.surface: An intellectual is struck by a sudden rush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'egghead' looks like a brainy person, but split it: the head of 'egg' gives E.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden headlong rush of a panicking herd or crowd is a mad dash.
